exposure: Binge alcohol exposure via gastric infusion
outcome: Fetal cerebral artery endocannabinoid system changes
Peak systolic blood velocity in middle cerebral arteries
Ethanol-induced dilation in fetal cerebral arteries
CB1 and CB2 receptor mRNA and protein levels
cohort: Pregnant baboons (Papio spp.) were used, with a control group infused with an isocaloric orange-flavored drink.
finding: Alcohol exposure during mid-pregnancy dilates fetal cerebral arteries via endocannabinoid receptors, specifically increasing the function of CB2.
followup_time: Observations were taken at a time equivalent to the end of the second trimester of human pregnancy.
gest_age: Exposure occurred three times during a period equivalent to the second trimester of human pregnancy; observations were made at a time equivalent to the end of the second trimester of human pregnancy.
